last.verdict: Opendoor is buying homes far faster than it sells them, and profit per sale is shrinking, so losses are set to widen.

takeaways.label: Margins missed, losses widen
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 12% to $1.02B, but contribution margin fell to 3.3% from 5.8% last quarter. That is below the 4%–4.5% guided in August. Net loss was $218M.

takeaways.label: Q4 guide is worse
takeaways.text: Management expects profit on homes sold to fall again in Q4 and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $70M–$85M, versus $31M this quarter. Revenue is guided up at least 40%.

takeaways.label: Inventory and debt pile up
takeaways.text: Opendoor bought 4,865 homes but sold 2,728, lifting inventory to $2.57B (7,596 homes). Bank debt secured by those homes is $2.4B, mostly due within a year; cash is $910M.

takeaways.label: Profit goal slipping
takeaways.text: The company says it is "behind" on its goal to reach positive adjusted net income by end of 2026, blaming a slower housing market, and intends to "catch up".

history.verdict: Investors sold on a weak margin outlook despite revenue and cash-burn improvement.

reasons.label: Lower margin outlook
reasons.text: Next-quarter contribution margin guided to 4%–4.5%, below this quarter's 5.8%, blamed on seasonality.

reasons.label: Sales far below last year
reasons.text: Revenue was $883M, down about 44% from a year ago, and below analyst estimates.

reasons.label: Bigger loss, mostly stock pay
reasons.text: Net loss was $162M versus $29M a year ago, driven by about $119M of stock-based pay.
